# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 48 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_048_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 5 — Closing Charge of the Mandates

**48:1** When I had finished writing all the commandments, he said to me: "I have now given you all these commandments; you shall keep them and walk in them. And you shall walk in them if your heart is pure toward God. And you shall keep them if you add no evil desire of the world to them — for it is not I who grants you this, but the Lord."

**48:2** "But if your heart is always directed toward God, all things are possible for you and you shall prevail over all these things. But if you turn away from God and waver, know that not a single one of these things will be possible for you. For the man who turns away from God will be unable to keep them and will be delivered over to death."

**48:3** "But I say to you, Hermas: these things I say to you are not my own words but the words of God whom I serve. Keep them and you shall live. I speak them not to you alone but to all who shall repent and perform these things."

**48:4** "For if you keep them you shall live and have peace with all people, and all who keep them shall have peace with one another. Therefore I charge you again: keep them diligently, obey them, and do not slacken your effort. For if you do these things you shall live; if you do not do them you shall die."

**48:5** When I had heard these commandments I departed from him greatly disturbed and afraid, and thought within myself: if even he who keeps the commandments shall with difficulty be saved, what shall become of those who do not keep them? And many anxieties and cares came upon me. But he said to me: "Do not be troubled by these things. Be strengthened and do good, and you shall receive great glory."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence in the solemn closing charge of the Mandates.*
